signature.name: Stated-limits accuracy
signature.description: The README tells a developer what the project will not do for them, in concrete, checkable terms that match the repository.

group-a.signature_why: Python 3.10, the demo refusing a non-empty workspace, and the transcribe dependencies all match run.py; the 3.10 floor itself is not enforced in code.
group-a.loved: The first screen shows the real report header and the README states plainly that the tool measures and checks but does not run a model.
group-a.docked: The opener is a dense paragraph before the clone command, so the first ten seconds are text-heavy.

group-b.signature_why: Limits section is specific (not access control, transcription does not identify speakers, ffmpeg and whisper.cpp needed) and all match the code; the 3.10 claim is unverified in code.
group-b.loved: The animated input-check-output reel shows a real quote going through the check, and the what-and-who sentence sits right under the title.
group-b.docked: The closing line saying the other commands were not run for the page undercuts the trust the rest of the page builds.

group-c.signature_why: Names the whisper-cli binary, the case-and-punctuation substring match, the missing speaker and context checks, and no CRM access; each matches run.py lines 144-161 and 270.
group-c.loved: The hook is concrete: three real transcript lines and a crop of the passing Quote verified result, with the limits stated right after.
group-c.docked: The How this README was checked block exposes check.log and claims.md, which is process leakage on a page meant for readers.
